key_insight: LLM-based agents must produce stable, consistent reasoning when faced with semantically equivalent input variations; the paper defines and operationalizes this property—"semantic invariance"—and shows that standard fixed-form benchmarks miss these reliability failures.
problem_solved: Addresses the gap in assurance that agentic LLMs reason consistently under paraphrases and other semantics-preserving input changes, revealing that canonical benchmark evaluations underrate brittleness in real-world, variable inputs.
method: Define the semantic invariance property and propose an evaluation protocol that measures consistency of agent outputs across semantically equivalent input perturbations.

Construct a suite of controlled semantic-preserving transformations (e.g., paraphrases, reordering, context framing) and apply them to agentic tasks (decision support, scientific reasoning, multi-agent coordination).
Introduce an invariance score/metric to quantify output stability and compare model behaviours to identify failure modes and mitigation opportunities.
impact: Provides practitioners with a practical way to detect and quantify brittle reasoning in agentic LLMs, enabling more reliable deployment in high-stakes settings and guiding robust model design and evaluation.
visual_elements: Pipeline diagram: diverse semantically equivalent inputs → LLM agent → aligned vs. divergent outputs (highlighting invariance failures).

paper_authors: I. de Zarzà, J. de Curtò, Jordi Cabot, Pietro Manzoni, Carlos T. Calafate
